record.context_brief: stochastic mirror descent rates for conjugate MAP on barrier objectives
record.original_question: View conjugate MAP estimation in an exponential family as stochastic mirror descent on the negative log-likelihood, with mirror map induced by the log-partition function A and decreasing step sizes γ_n = 1/(n_0 + n). Find a convergence-rate theorem for stochastic mirror descent that is strong enough to cover the MAP iterates arising from standard exponential-family models, including Gaussian examples such as N(m, σ^2) or the barrier-type case N(0, σ^2), despite the fact that existing relative-smoothness analyses fail on these barrier objectives. In particular, the desired result should explain the observed O(1/n) behavior for MAP-like updates in settings where current SMD bounds do not apply.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2 (Convergence rate for SMD). Find a convergence rate for stochastic mirror descent that applies to conjugate MAP of exponential families such as Gaussians N (μ, σ2).
Proving convergence of stochastic mirror descent on barrier loss remains an open problem.
Nevertheless, none of the current analyses of SMD hold for the MAP, even on a simple family such as N (0, σ2), thus revealing an area for progress in non-Euclidean optimization.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ be a regular exponential family on a sample space $\mathcal{X}$ with natural parameter $\theta\in\Theta\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$, sufficient statistic $T:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^d$, base measure $\nu$, and log-partition function $A(\theta)=\log\int_{\mathcal{X}} e^{\langle\theta,T(x)\rangle}\,d\nu(x)$, so that the density is $p_\theta(x)=\exp(\langle\theta,T(x)\rangle - A(\theta))$. The function $A$ is strictly convex and smooth on the interior of $\Theta$, and serves as a Legendre-type mirror map; let $D_A(\theta,\theta')=A(\theta)-A(\theta')-\langle\nabla A(\theta'),\theta-\theta'\rangle$ denote the associated Bregman divergence.

Given i.i.d.\ observations $X_1,X_2,\dots$ from $P_{\theta^\star}$ and a conjugate prior with hyperparameters $(\chi,n_0)$, the conjugate MAP recursion can be written as the stochastic mirror descent iteration
$$\nabla A(\theta_{n+1}) = \nabla A(\theta_n) - \gamma_n\,\widehat{g}_n,\qquad \gamma_n=\frac{1}{n_0+n},$$
where $\widehat{g}_n=\nabla A(\theta_n)-T(X_{n+1})$ is an unbiased stochastic (sub)gradient of the negative log-likelihood objective $F(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{X\sim P_{\theta^\star}}[-\log p_\theta(X)]$.

Problem. Establish a non-asymptotic convergence-rate theorem for stochastic mirror descent with mirror map $A$, step sizes $\gamma_n=1/(n_0+n)$, and unbiased stochastic gradients of $F$, that
(i) applies to conjugate MAP iterates for standard exponential families, including Gaussian models such as $\mathcal{N}(m,\sigma^2)$ with unknown mean and the barrier-type model $\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2)$ with unknown variance, in regimes where $F$ is not relatively smooth with respect to $A$ on the closure of the iterates' domain (so that existing relative-smoothness based SMD analyses do not apply); and
(ii) yields a rate of the form $\mathbb{E}[F(\theta_n)-F(\theta^\star)]=O(1/n)$ (or $\mathbb{E}[D_A(\theta^\star,\theta_n)]=O(1/n)$), matching the empirically observed behavior of MAP estimators in these models.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem. Existing stochastic mirror descent analyses rely on uniform relative-smoothness assumptions that fail for barrier-type objectives such as the negative log-likelihood of $\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2)$, where iterates can approach the boundary of the domain. Recent related works on SMD and natural-gradient variational inference have made partial progress (e.g., geometric convergence to a neighborhood, or rates under stronger assumptions) but no published result yet establishes a general $O(1/n)$ rate covering MAP iterates in all standard exponential-family/Gaussian barrier examples.

status_evidence.title: Convergence Rates for the MAP of an Exponential Family and Stochastic Mirror Descent -- an Open Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Modern convergence results do not apply for standard examples of the exponential family, highlighting holes in the convergence literature.
status_evidence.claim: The convergence rate for SMD on conjugate MAP of standard exponential families is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On Stochastic Mirror Descent: Convergence Analysis and Adaptive Variants
status_evidence.snippet: Existing analyses assume bounds hold uniformly for every iterate, but for barrier objectives a uniform bound over iterates cannot hold.
status_evidence.claim: Barrier objectives violate the uniform relative-smoothness assumptions used in current SMD convergence analyses.
